title: Firefly III
name: firefly-iii
description: Personal finance manager for tracking what comes in and goes out, with budgets, subscriptions, recurring transactions, rules and reports. This one runs on Postgres. Source: https://github.com/firefly-iii/firefly-iii

env.name: FIREFLY_APP_KEY
env.label: App key (required)
env.description: Exactly 32 characters. Generate one with: openssl rand -hex 16. Keep it the same when you redeploy, or everyone's logged out and API tokens stop working.

env.name: FIREFLY_CRON_TOKEN
env.label: Cron token (required)
env.description: Exactly 32 characters, and not the same as the app key. Generate one with: openssl rand -hex 16.

env.name: FIREFLY_DB_PASSWORD
env.label: Database password (required)
env.description: Generate one with: openssl rand -hex 32. Keep it the same when you redeploy, or Firefly III can't reach its database.

env.name: FIREFLY_PORT
env.label: Host port for the web UI

env.name: FIREFLY_TZ
env.label: Timezone
env.description: Like Europe/London. Transaction dates and the nightly cron use it.

env.name: FIREFLY_TRUSTED_PROXIES
env.label: Trusted proxies
env.description: Leave blank, unless it's behind a reverse proxy. Then set ** so Firefly III trusts the proxy's headers.

note: Fill in all three secrets before you deploy, since the stack won't start without them. The app key and cron token must be exactly 32 characters (openssl rand -hex 16 makes one), and keep all three the same when you redeploy. Then open http://<your-host>:8092 (or whichever port you picked) and register. The first account becomes the admin and sign-ups close after it, so do it straight away. A small cron container pings Firefly III at 03:00 every night, which is what creates recurring transactions and fires subscription reminders. Transactions live in Postgres, in the postgres-data volume, and attachments in firefly-upload. Docs: docs.firefly-iii.org
